notes: Every generated task says why it exists. If one is wrong, delete it: the checklist will not put it back.
A task's due date moves when the event date moves. A task you have ticked stays ticked.

tasks.detail: Pick the main date, and a fallback in case the venue falls through. Write both down.
tasks.title: Fix the date and the second date

tasks.derivation: every event needs a head count
tasks.detail: A working number, not a final one. Most of the hall's numbers follow from it.
tasks.title: Agree the guest count

tasks.detail: One figure, and the ten per cent that stays in reserve.
tasks.title: Lock the budget

tasks.detail: Who is covered for what, and what the venue requires from you in writing.
tasks.mitigation: Venue public liability; vendor PL certificates for all suppliers; an event policy for cancellation and supplier failure, checked 6 weeks out.
tasks.title: Check the venue and event insurance

tasks.detail: Confirm capacity, access times, power, toilets and what happens if it rains.
tasks.mitigation: Compare the final RSVP against the written capacity; hold a 5–10 % buffer; name an overflow room.
tasks.title: Sign the venue contract

tasks.detail: Caterer, photographer, DJ or band, and the décor house. In that order in December.
tasks.mitigation: A cancellation clause with a refund schedule; a tight force-majeure; a backup list of 2 vendors per category.
tasks.title: Book the core vendors

tasks.detail: A deposit without a receipt is a gift. Keep them together in one place.
tasks.mitigation: Pay by card; staged payments, no more than 50 % before the event; verify registration; event insurance covering supplier failure.
tasks.title: Pay the deposits, and get receipts

tasks.detail: Agree the portion size per guest, and whether the vendor plates or serves.
tasks.mitigation: A guaranteed headcount plus 5–10 %; model plated against buffet; count vendor and crew meals.
tasks.title: Do the tasting, and agree portions

tasks.detail: The list of must-have shots, and who from the family is in them.
tasks.title: Agree the photography brief

tasks.detail: Confirm 30 table linens and the colour they will be
tasks.title: Confirm 30 table linens

tasks.detail: One centrepiece per table, plus two spare for the high table. Order 30 and keep the spares in a box.
tasks.title: Book 30 centrepieces

tasks.derivation: because the plan runs on a generator
tasks.detail: Price the litres for the full run plus the load-in, and agree who delivers them. A generator with an empty tank is a generator.
tasks.mitigation: Size with 30–40 % headroom; fuel for the day plus 4 hours; a second smaller backup; service log.
tasks.title: Book the fuel, not just the generator

tasks.derivation: because the plan runs on a generator
tasks.detail: A second set, or a clear answer about which circuits go dark. Write the answer down.
tasks.mitigation: Dual supply; UPS on sound and AV; rehearse the changeover 2 times.
tasks.title: Name the backup

tasks.detail: One station per 60 guests, chafing dishes priced in, and enough aisle that the queue does not block the dance floor.
tasks.title: Plan the buffet stations and the queue

tasks.detail: 300 guests needs more toilets than the venue will admit to having. Count them on a site visit and hire the shortfall.
tasks.mitigation: Ratio check; at least one accessible unit; one attendant per 2 units, with consumables.
tasks.title: Check the toilet ratio

tasks.derivation: every event has a guest list
tasks.detail: One list, one link, and a reply-by date the caterer can hold you to.
tasks.title: Send the invitations

tasks.derivation: seating cannot start before replies close
tasks.detail: Chase the undecided once, then count what you have.
tasks.mitigation: A 10 % RSVP buffer; overflow seating; a standing area; a second room.
tasks.title: Close the replies

tasks.derivation: because your hall has 30 tables and 300 guests
tasks.detail: The hall plan seats 300 guests across 30 tables. Check the party sizes and the family groupings before you lock it.
tasks.title: Seat 300 guests across 30 tables

tasks.derivation: because your plan has a dance floor
tasks.detail: A floor on soft ground or over a bund sinks by the second set. Ask the venue where the slab ends.
tasks.mitigation: Ask for floor loading figures; spread heavy items; cap raised staging at 4 people per m².
tasks.title: Check the dance floor goes on solid ground

tasks.derivation: every event has guests who need it
tasks.detail: Steps at the entrance, a toilet someone can reach, and a seat for an elder who cannot stand long.
tasks.mitigation: A step-free route; one accessible toilet; 2 reserved seats per 50 guests; MC and sign-language provision.
tasks.title: Walk the room for accessibility

tasks.detail: Who is driving, who is not, and how the last guests get home.
tasks.mitigation: A confirmed fleet with driver contacts; one spare vehicle; departures staggered 15 minutes apart; a return schedule.
tasks.title: Plan the transport home

tasks.derivation: every event needs a run sheet
tasks.detail: Times, who gives each signal, and the number for every vendor.
tasks.mitigation: A run sheet with a 10-minute buffer between segments; hard stops; the MC has written authority to cut.
tasks.title: Write the run sheet

tasks.detail: Time, address, load-in door, contact number. One message each.
tasks.mitigation: A written setup window and venue access time; a 2-hour buffer before guest arrival.
tasks.title: Confirm every vendor, in writing

tasks.derivation: because the plan runs on a generator
tasks.detail: Oil, filters, and a run under the plan's real load. Do it a week out, so a fault still has time to be fixed.
tasks.mitigation: Size with 30–40 % headroom; fuel for the day plus 4 hours; a second smaller backup; service log.
tasks.title: Have the generator serviced and test-loaded

tasks.detail: Above 250 guests the room needs someone whose only job is medical. Confirm they carry a kit and know where the nearest hospital is.
tasks.mitigation: One first-aider per 250 guests; the AED location; an ambulance access route; the nearest hospital printed.
tasks.title: Book a first-aider for the full day

tasks.detail: Match the number to the crowd and the car park, and agree radio channels with the venue.
tasks.mitigation: One vetted guard per 100 guests; a guest list at the gate; a bag policy; a secure point for gifts and cash.
tasks.title: Book extra security for the gates and the gifts

tasks.detail: Rain, heat, wind. Decide now whether the plan changes.
tasks.mitigation: A covered route between ceremony and reception; an indoor fallback of equal capacity; drainage; umbrellas for 1 in 5 guests.
tasks.title: Read the five-day forecast

tasks.derivation: because your date falls in the harmattan
tasks.detail: Dust settles on linen and in eyes, and drops the evening temperature. Plan covers, lip balm for the bridal party, and a gentle rehydration station.
tasks.mitigation: Prefer indoor or covered; dust covers for cake and plated food; seal AV; warn guests 72 hours out about visibility, travel delays, dry eyes and respiratory effects.
tasks.title: Read the harmattan forecast

tasks.derivation: the network may not reach the venue
tasks.detail: Two copies: one for the venue, one for you. A phone dies on the day.
tasks.mitigation: A run sheet with a 10-minute buffer between segments; hard stops; the MC has written authority to cut.
tasks.title: Print the run sheet and the seating plan

tasks.derivation: the day starts with a briefing
tasks.detail: One page, one walk through the room, every name and number read out.
tasks.title: Brief the team

tasks.detail: The times that cannot move: caterer on site, guests in, cake, last set.
tasks.mitigation: A run sheet with a 10-minute buffer between segments; hard stops; the MC has written authority to cut.
tasks.title: Hold the hard stops

tasks.detail: Whatever came from the venue or the décor house goes back, and the deposit comes with it.
tasks.mitigation: Pay by card; staged payments, no more than 50 % before the event; verify registration; event insurance covering supplier failure.
tasks.title: Return the hired things

tasks.derivation: the people who helped deserve a note
tasks.detail: To the vendors, and to the family who carried the day.
tasks.title: Send the thank-you notes

tasks.derivation: final invoices land after the day
tasks.detail: Every final invoice, paid and filed where you can find it.
tasks.mitigation: An itemised quote; an all-in comparison of 3 quotes; overtime and power rates in writing.
tasks.title: Clear the balances

tasks.derivation: vendor trust is built by reviews
tasks.detail: A line each. It helps the next couple, and it helps you remember.
tasks.title: Review the vendors you would book again
